title: Desertion as a divorce ground - how long must it actually last
p1:
Many people think that if a spouse leaves home, divorce can happen immediately. But the law does not always see leaving as desertion.

The real question is: how long must someone stay away before it becomes a legal ground for divorce?
p2: A common misconception is that any separation counts as desertion. In many Indian divorce laws, desertion generally means a continuous period of at least two years where one spouse has abandoned the other without a reasonable cause and without the intention to return.
p3:
The surprising part? Physical distance alone is not enough. Courts also look at the intention behind the separation. Someone living separately due to work, safety concerns, or a temporary dispute may not be considered a deserter.

The practical takeaway: the timeline matters, but the reason and intention behind the separation can decide the outcome.
conclusion: Did you know that simply living apart does not automatically qualify as desertion for divorce? What factor do you think matters more: the time apart or the reason behind it?
